title: Currently new at RPG Maker and trying to train myself to use it. Got any advice ?

posts.author: Xelarande
posts.body:
Hi !
I'm new here, and also new to RPG Maker (well not really, I spent 2 months trying to use the lite version of VX Ace, but still).
Recently managed to get the full version, it's really cool !
I'm currently trying to develop something, and since I assume it's gonna take me some time, I wondered if you have any recommendations or advises for a beginner ?
Thank you !

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
I once wrote the "starting point" tutorial linked in my signature for new users.
It was written for VXA but is mostly valid for MV and MZ as well
other than that, go through the build-in tutorial and read through the help file

posts.author: Timeline_man
posts.body:
If you have any interest in finishing anything, start small, grow slowly.
consult the help file, then Google, then the forum for the smoothest way to learn things and solve problems
don't drown yourself in planned features
accept any feedback, good or bad, with grace

posts.author: DrFreeman
posts.body:
The old way that people learned RPG Maker (RPGM) was to imitate demo scenes from other games then they had fully fleshed out their own game once they understood how to do the mechanics. But this was the method they used like 20 years ago. Don Miguel convinced me to buy like 4 versions of RPG Maker . I think the new way that many people learn RPGM is to follow the tutorials, experiment, build small projects, and then build for jams.  Maybe someone might have a more structured input for modern learning, but
this is the tutorial on how to use RPG Maker VX Ace
. The newer tutorial
area is here
. There are some books on Amazon you can buy or you can use a Skillsoft license to read them. I found a book
Beginning RPG Maker VX Ace
that you could check the sample and see if you like it. There are also quite a few tutorials (playlists) on Youtube to follow too.
My advice is:
Build with purpose to satisfy yourself and others
Learn from the greats
Practice makes perfect
Use your drive and discipline
Find your limit and the technologies limit

posts.author: kirbwarrior
posts.body:
When you first get a new tool, you want to know what it can and can't do, what is reasonable, and what things mean. Poke around events and see what each event command does, look at the premade maps and check out how tilesets work when making maps. There's help documentation, built in tutorials, and online tutorials. You should definitely have one project that is just tinkering with the system to learn things.
Then it's a good idea to
start small
. We ALL have be drawn to the idea of big, sprawling games, but it's important to make
any
game just to get an idea of what it means to make one. A single map with a few encounters can give you a bite-sized chunk of an RPG and you'll understand so much from spending that time making it.

posts.author: TeiRaven
posts.body:
Welcome aboard! Congrats on getting VX Ace, I think you'll enjoy the freedom it offers compared to VXA Lite. You've gotten lots of good advice here already! My advice for starting out and learning: have fun! If you're enjoying what you're doing, you're naturally going to want to learn how to do more.
Tutorials are great, but take care to not get bogged down by them. By which I mean: if the tutorial is telling you to map a knight encampment, but you would rather map Granny's cottage and garden, you should try it. Let the tutorials be your travel guidebook, not your entire itinerary. You'll still learn!
My very first RPG Maker project was basically a small apartment building, with few studio apartments for a handful of characters. It was an exercise in how to use the mapping system, how to build and import my own tilesets, and how to use basic event commands. There were doors, there were people to talk to, there were chests to open and key items to interact with--not exactly complex gameplay, but I enjoyed the learning process and it was effective for me.
(As an aside: the Help files are an incredible resource, and they should be the first place you look when you have a question! "How do I change the font color? How do I import a character? How big is a tileset?" are all the types of questions that you should consult the help file for. But I don't think it's necessary or practical to read the entire thing front to back before you even begin. I certainly never have!)

posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body:
Welcome to the forum and congrats on starting down the glorious path of game making!
In addition to what has already been suggested, I will just summarize what I did when I first started about 3 years ago with MZ.
If there is a built in tutorial in VX Ace, do that.
Search YouTube for "RPG Maker VX Ace Tutorials" and you will find entire playlists.
Recreate a bunch of those tutorials that cover the basics to more advanced concepts (don't just watch them...recreate them in your own testing project).
Read through the Help documentation.
Go through everything in the Event Command menus to learn how everything works.
Start experimenting with making things that interest you to learn functionality.
If you really love a few particular games, see if you can recreate parts of those games to see if you can get the functionality to work.
If you have questions, try to search the internet for the answer. If you can't find anything, then post on the forum.
Finally, make a very short end to end game experience. VERY small. Just to learn all the steps in making, testing, and deploying a game.
I would do all this before I started exploring what plugins can offer.
Then you can experiment with plugins and start collecting free assets to use in future projects.
Anyway, those steps have served me pretty well.
I have been doing this for about 3 years, I think I have made some great progress, and I still haven't explored plugins other than a couple of default ones that come with MZ and a couple of very short custom plugins that users here have offered as solutions to questions that I posed. Depending on the type of game you want to make, you can do so much without ever using additional plugins.
Good luck on your projects!
